## Dates

Each commit is dated at noon (America/Bogota) on the day the change took effect. The other dates, enacted and published, are trailers.

When a law gives no date of its own, the default rule applies: Ley 4 de 1913 (Código de Régimen Político y Municipal), arts. 52 and 53: a law binds two months after its promulgation unless it fixes its own day. Actos Legislativos (amendments to the Constitution) state their own vigencia, almost always 'rige a partir de su publicación'. http://www.secretariasenado.gov.co/senado/basedoc/ley_0004_1913.html

## How the history is built

`tools/build.py` turns the corpus into this history in one pass: one commit per law, on the day it took effect. The same corpus always gives the same commit hashes. `tools/check_repo.py` reads every version back from git and compares it with the corpus. `tools/on.py` shows the law as it stood on any date. The corpus format is described in `tools/SCHEMA.md`.

## Decisions made by hand

- Source: the Secretaría General del Senado's basedoc, the only free official-site source that keeps each provision's earlier texts ('Legislación Anterior'). SUIN-Juriscol (Ministerio de Justicia) does not give earlier texts.
- Versions are rebuilt per provision from the source's earlier texts ('Texto original de la Constitución Política:', 'Texto modificado por el Acto Legislativo N de AAAA:'), its inline amendment markers ('<Inciso adicionado por el artículo 1 del Acto Legislativo 1 de 2005 ...>') and its Notas de Vigencia. A part marked 'adicionado' did not exist before the act that added it.
- In-force days: an Acto Legislativo takes effect on the day of its publication in the Diario Oficial, as the source's notes state ('Rige a partir de su publicación'), unless the note quotes another vigencia clause: Acto Legislativo 1 de 2001 from 1 January 2002, Actos Legislativos 1 and 4 de 2007 from 1 January 2008, and the election-day clauses of Actos Legislativos 2 de 2005 (12 March 2006), 3 de 2005 (14 March 2010) and 3 de 2007 (28 October 2007).
- Election days are taken from Registraduría Nacional del Estado Civil pages, not written by hand: 12 March 2006 from 'Calendario Electoral 2006 - 2010' (Resolución 0497 de 2005), https://www.registraduria.gov.co/Calendario-Electoral-2006-2010.html; 14 March 2010 from Comunicado de Prensa No. 050 de 2009, https://web.archive.org/web/20110726040247id_/http://www.registraduria.gov.co/ESTA-LISTO-EL-PRE-CALENDARIO.html; 28 October 2007 from the Registraduría home page as captured on 30 September 2007 ('el proceso electoral del 28 de octubre'; the year is the capture's), https://web.archive.org/web/20070930160642id_/http://www.registraduria.gov.co/. All three agree with the days used before.
- Acto Legislativo 3 de 2002 says it 'rige a partir de su aprobación' and applies gradually from 2005; its text changes are dated from its publication (20 December 2002).
- Constitutional Court rulings that struck text (INEXEQUIBLE) are laws of kind 'court', dated by the day of the ruling as the source gives it (rulings take effect from their date unless the Court says otherwise, Ley 270 de 1996 art. 45). When a whole Acto Legislativo was struck, the provision returns to its text before that act. Struck words shown in the current text are in force until the ruling and removed from it.
- Rulings that upheld text on a condition of interpretation (exequibilidad condicionada) change no words: they are court laws with a note, credited to the provision on the ruling's day. Plain EXEQUIBLE rulings, inhibitions and 'estarse a lo resuelto' rulings are not recorded.
- The first version is the 1991 Constitution as the source gives it: the second corrected edition (Gaceta Constitucional No. 116 of 20 July 1991), dated from promulgation on 4 July 1991 (art. 380). The 1991 Aclaración published in Gaceta Constitucional No. 125 is its own commit, kind 'decree'.
- Where the source names an act that changed a provision but does not give the text in force after it (a later act changed the same words again), that act and the next one with a known text are credited together on the later day.
- Avance Jurídico's editorial notes and markers (<...>) are not part of the text. The article heading is written as '# Art. N'; the heading of books, titles and chapters are kept in titulos.md, a heading shown while an article under it exists.
- Placeholder line: where the source names the act that changed a provision but gives no text in force after it (or no 1991 text), the provision reads '[La fuente no da el texto vigente en esta fecha.]' for that period, credited to the act named. Cases: art-122 from 1991-07-04, art-122 from 1991-09-25, art-122 from 2004-01-08, art-256 from 2015-07-01, art-263 from 1991-07-04, art-322 from 1991-07-04, art-328 from 2007-07-06, art-361 from 2011-07-18.
- Approximations, from the source's own notes: 241: struck text but no dated ruling; struck text dropped from all versions; 250: slot chain ends on a text other than today's; today's text used from 2011-11-24; 328: al-2-2017 marked INEXEQUIBLE but no dated ruling found; TRANSITORIO ACL02021-5: slot chain ends on a text other than today's; today's text used from 2021-08-25.
- Headings (titulos.md): the publisher's page links 'Anterior | Siguiente' that the basedoc prints after the last heading of a page are not words of that heading and are left out.
- Dated-struck audit, hand entries (2026-10-31): words the page shows struck or replaced, which the engine had left out of the versions they belong to (the text before the change differs from today's, the source's earlier text was not known, or the page marks a substitution), were put back by hand from the page's own struck words, notes and rulings box, each in the versions its entry names; on the day the page gives they go or change, credited to the ruling or act that made the change: Constitución Política de Colombia 1991 art. 241: the last numeral ('Darse su propio reglamento') is numbered 11 from 1991-07-04 until Acto Legislativo 2 de 2015 added a numeral 11 and it became 12 (the page shows the old number struck).
- Box text (2026-11-01): publisher box text the source page prints inside an article was stored as the article's words; taken out of every version, every kept word checked on the act's own pages or the credited law's: constitucion art-052, art-233.
- Later parágrafo lines (2026-11-01): where a later act added a parágrafo of several lines, the page marks only its first line as added, and its other lines had stood in the versions before that act; they now start with the parágrafo, on the act's day: Constitución Política de Colombia 1991 art. 48 (1991-07-04); Constitución Política de Colombia 1991 art. 152 (1991-07-04); Constitución Política de Colombia 1991 art. 347 (1991-07-04).
- Código Civil and Ley 1581 de 2012: source is the Secretaría General del Senado's basedoc, the only free official source that keeps each article's earlier texts ('Legislación Anterior').
- Código Civil: versions are rebuilt per article from the source's earlier texts ('Texto original del Código Civil:', 'Texto modificado por la Ley 1a. de 1976:'), its inline amendment markers ('<Artículo modificado por el artículo 1o. del Decreto 2820 de 1974 ...>') and its Notas de Vigencia. A part marked 'adicionado' did not exist before the act that added it.
- Código Civil: the first version is Ley 84 de 1873 (the code of the United States of Colombia), dated from its sanction on 26 May 1873 because the source gives no other day; Ley 57 de 1887 adopted it for the Republic from 90 days after its own publication (19 July 1887), with the reforms it made.
- Código Civil: derogations the source calls tacit ('derogado tácitamente', 'orgánicamente') change no text and are not recorded; only express changes are.
- Código Civil: the notes cite the Código de Procedimiento Civil and the Código Sustantivo del Trabajo by name; they are Decreto 1400 de 1970 and Decreto 2663 de 1950.
- In-force days of amending acts: the act's own vigencia clause as its basedoc page gives it, or as the Código Civil page quotes it; a day that a provision's own note gives ('La derogatoria rige a partir del 1o. de enero de 2014') applies to that provision. Acts the basedoc does not hold (most acts before 1992) are dated by the default rule: before 1913, from publication in the Diario Oficial (Código Civil arts. 11 and 12); from 1913, two months after it (Ley 4 de 1913, art. 52). The list below gives the day and the rule for each act.
- Typing slips in the source, corrected: 'Ley 25 de 1892' (its note gives the Diario Oficial of 18 December 1992) is Ley 25 de 1992; 'Ley 2820 de 1974' is Decreto 2820 de 1974; 'Ley 95 de 1980' in art. 217's earlier text is Ley 95 de 1890 (the reform of arts. 214-217 that Ley 1060 de 2006 later repealed as 'los artículos 5o y 6o de la Ley 95 de 1890'); the Colpensiones heading of Ley 8 de 1922 dates its Diario Oficial No. 18.199bis to 23 February 1913, read as 1922.
- Old acts the basedoc does not hold are read, for their heading and vigencia clause only, from the same Avance Jurídico compilation as published by Colpensiones (normativa.colpensiones.gov.co).
- Where the source shows words struck as INEXEQUIBLE but names no dated ruling for them (arts. 669, 1119, 1527), the struck words are left out of every version; art. 312's struck text is likewise left out.
- Today's text on the source page is taken as the text in force now; where an earlier-text box gives the same act's wording slightly differently (art. 200), the page's current text wins. - Headings (titulos.md): the publisher's page links 'Anterior | Siguiente' that the basedoc prints after the last heading of a page are not words of that heading and are left out.
- Signature blocks at the end of the last article ('El Presidente del Honorable Senado de la República, ...', 'La Presidenta del honorable Senado ...', 'Publíquese y cúmplase. Dado en ...') are not part of the text and are cut: ley-1581-2012 art-0030.
- Código Civil: article words the page puts under anchors named like headings ('Nivel001', 'TITULO I', ...) had been read as headings, so they were missing from their articles (in titulos.md, or nowhere); they are back in them: art. 642 (its heading in the text, under an anchor named 'Nivel001').
- Shared law notes (2026-11-01): Decreto 538 de 2020, art. 8, limited literal g) of Ley 1581 de 2012 art. 4 (security of data) to the technical, human and administrative security measures of health providers while the COVID-19 health emergency lasted, from 2020-04-12; it changed no words of LPDP Art. 4. The decree changes words of other acts, so its law entry carries no note.
- Shared law notes (2026-11-01): Sentencia C-039 de 2025 upheld these provisions on a condition of interpretation (exequibilidad condicionada) and changed no words of them: CC Art. 140 on 2025-02-05. The ruling changes words elsewhere, so its law entry carries no note.
- Shared law entries (2026-11-01): Ley 11 de 1984: published 1984-03-05 (Diario Oficial No. 36.517 of 5 March 1984, as the Código Sustantivo del Trabajo's notes give it; a copy of the act heads it '30 de abril de 1984', which the Diario Oficial's numbering rules out (No. 36.450 of 17 January 1984, No. 36.608 of 14 May 1984)); every part of this corpus now gives that day (this part had 1984-04-30).
- Box text (2026-11-01): publisher box text the source page prints inside an article was stored as the article's words; taken out of every version, every kept word checked on the act's own pages or the credited law's: codigo-civil art-1624.
- Default-date audit (2026-11-01): Ley 75 de 1968: published 1968-12-31 (the act's own heading: 'Diario Oficial No. 32.682 de 31 de diciembre de 1968') (this part had 1968-12-21).
- Código Penal, Código General del Proceso: versions are rebuilt per article from the basedoc's earlier texts, inline amendment markers and Notas de Vigencia, as for the Constitution and the Código Civil. Where the source names an act but gives no text after it, the article reads '[La fuente no da el texto vigente en esta fecha.]' for that period.
- Constitutional Court rulings that struck text are laws of kind 'court', dated by the ruling's day as the source gives it; rulings that upheld text on a condition are court laws with a note and change no words.
- In-force days of amending acts: the act's own vigencia clause as its basedoc page gives it; otherwise the default rule (Ley 4 de 1913, art. 52: two months after promulgation). A day a provision's own note gives applies to that provision. The list below gives the day and the rule for each act.
- Dates come only from the act itself: the Diario Oficial day on the act's own page wins over a day the code's notes give; a note's Diario Oficial day is not given to an act named only inside another act's quoted title; and an act whose vigencia clause has a general rule and exceptions is dated by the rule that covers the changed provision (Ley 890 de 2004: arts. 7 to 13 immediately, the rest from 1 January 2005; Ley 2502 de 2025: art. 296 of the Código Penal one year after promulgation; Ley 2080 de 2021: from publication).
- The source's earlier texts often leave out the article's epigraph (its title); where the latest earlier text differs from today's only by that or by a change no note names, today's text is used from the latest named act's day. Articles where that happened: ley_0599_2000 art-0058, ley_0599_2000 art-0215, ley_0599_2000 art-0312, ley_0599_2000 art-0337, ley_0599_2000 art-0471, ley_1564_2012 art-0020, ley_1564_2012 art-0024, ley_1564_2012 art-0338, ley_1564_2012 art-0393, ley_1564_2012 art-0397, ley_1564_2012 art-0553, ley_1564_2012 art-0625, ley_1564_2012 art-0626, ley_1564_2012 art-0627.
- Código Penal: the figures of the penalties in the Parte Especial after 1 January 2005 are the publisher's: Ley 890 de 2004, art. 14, raised every penalty of the Parte Especial by a third in the minimum and a half in the maximum without rewriting the articles, and the source shows each article 'con las penas aumentadas' under the marker '<Penas aumentadas por el artículo 14 de la Ley 890 de 2004, a partir del 1o. de enero de 2005>', with the earlier wording in its Legislación Anterior. Those changes are credited to Ley 890 de 2004 on 1 January 2005; the source's own warning says the computation is the editor's reading of art. 14.
- Código General del Proceso: its first version is dated from promulgation (2012-07-12), the day the first of its articles took effect under art. 627 num. 1; the article itself (in the text) gives the later starts of the rest. Splitting the first version by article would need the Consejo Superior de la Judicatura's district-by-district acts, which the source does not give.

Ley 171 de 1961 is in force from 1 February 1962 (its art. 15: 'desde el día 1o. del mes siguiente al de su promulgación'; Diario Oficial No. 30.696 of 16 January 1962 in the source's notes).

El texto derogado continua vigente para los trabajadores sometidos al régimen de transición creado por el artículo 36 de la Ley 100. El texto original es el es el siguiente:>' or '<Artículo subrogado por La ley 100 de 1993. Ver Notas del Editor. El texto original es el siguiente:>'. Those words are read as the articles' original text, and the articles are removed on Ley 100's in-force day, like arts. 268 to 272 that the same act repealed. - Código Nacional de Seguridad y Convivencia Ciudadana, Ley 100 de 1993, Código General Disciplinario, Código Electoral: versions are rebuilt per article from the basedoc's earlier texts, inline amendment markers and Notas de Vigencia, as for the Constitution and the Código Civil. Where the source names an act but gives no text after it, the article reads '[La fuente no da el texto vigente en esta fecha.]' for that period.
- Constitutional Court rulings that struck text are laws of kind 'court', dated by the ruling's day as the source gives it; rulings that upheld text on a condition are court laws with a note and change no words.
- In-force days of amending acts: the act's own vigencia clause as its basedoc page gives it; otherwise the default rule (Ley 4 de 1913, art. 52: two months after promulgation). A day a provision's own note gives applies to that provision. The list below gives the day and the rule for each act.
- Dates come only from the act itself: the Diario Oficial day on the act's own page wins over a day the code's notes give; a note's Diario Oficial day is not given to an act named only inside another act's quoted title; and an act whose vigencia clause has a general rule and exceptions is dated by the rule that covers the changed provision (Ley 890 de 2004: arts. 7 to 13 immediately, the rest from 1 January 2005; Ley 2502 de 2025: art. 296 of the Código Penal one year after promulgation; Ley 2080 de 2021: from publication).

- Estatuto Tributario, Estatuto General de Contratación, Estatuto del Consumidor, Código Nacional de Tránsito: versions are rebuilt per article from the basedoc's earlier texts, inline amendment markers and Notas de Vigencia, as for the Constitution and the Código Civil. Where the source names an act but gives no text after it, the article reads '[La fuente no da el texto vigente en esta fecha.]' for that period.
- Constitutional Court rulings that struck text are laws of kind 'court', dated by the ruling's day as the source gives it; rulings that upheld text on a condition are court laws with a note and change no words.
- In-force days of amending acts: the act's own vigencia clause as its basedoc page gives it; otherwise the default rule (Ley 4 de 1913, art. 52: two months after promulgation). A day a provision's own note gives applies to that provision. The list below gives the day and the rule for each act.
- Dates come only from the act itself: the Diario Oficial day on the act's own page wins over a day the code's notes give; a note's Diario Oficial day is not given to an act named only inside another act's quoted title; and an act whose vigencia clause has a general rule and exceptions is dated by the rule that covers the changed provision (Ley 890 de 2004: arts. 7 to 13 immediately, the rest from 1 January 2005; Ley 2502 de 2025: art. 296 of the Código Penal one year after promulgation; Ley 2080 de 2021: from publication).

Where the source names an act but gives no text after it, the article reads '[La fuente no da el texto vigente en esta fecha.]' for that period.
- Constitutional Court rulings that struck text are laws of kind 'court', dated by the ruling's day as the source gives it; rulings that upheld text on a condition are court laws with a note and change no words.
- In-force days of amending acts: the act's own vigencia clause as its basedoc page gives it; otherwise the default rule (Ley 4 de 1913, art. 52: two months after promulgation). A day a provision's own note gives applies to that provision. The list below gives the day and the rule for each act.
- Dates come only from the act itself: the Diario Oficial day on the act's own page wins over a day the code's notes give; a note's Diario Oficial day is not given to an act named only inside another act's quoted title; and an act whose vigencia clause has a general rule and exceptions is dated by the rule that covers the changed provision (Ley 890 de 2004: arts. 7 to 13 immediately, the rest from 1 January 2005; Ley 2502 de 2025: art. 296 of the Código Penal one year after promulgation; Ley 2080 de 2021: from publication).
- The source's earlier texts often leave out the article's epigraph (its title); where the latest earlier text differs from today's only by that or by a change no note names, today's text is used from the latest named act's day. - Constitutional Court rulings that struck text are laws of kind 'court', dated by the ruling's day as the source gives it; rulings that upheld text on a condition are court laws with a note and change no words.
- In-force days of amending acts: the act's own vigencia clause as its basedoc page gives it; otherwise the default rule (Ley 4 de 1913, art. 52: two months after promulgation). A day a provision's own note gives applies to that provision. The list below gives the day and the rule for each act.

Where the source names an act but gives no text after it, the article reads '[La fuente no da el texto vigente en esta fecha.]' for that period.
- Constitutional Court rulings that struck text are laws of kind 'court', dated by the ruling's day as the source gives it; rulings that upheld text on a condition are court laws with a note and change no words.
- In-force days of amending acts: the act's own vigencia clause as its basedoc page gives it; otherwise the default rule (Ley 4 de 1913, art. 52: two months after promulgation). A day a provision's own note gives applies to that provision. The list below gives the day and the rule for each act.
- Dates come only from the act itself: the Diario Oficial day on the act's own page wins over a day the code's notes give; a note's Diario Oficial day is not given to an act named only inside another act's quoted title; and an act whose vigencia clause has a general rule and exceptions is dated by the rule that covers the changed provision (Ley 890 de 2004: arts. 7 to 13 immediately, the rest from 1 January 2005; Ley 2502 de 2025: art. 296 of the Código Penal one year after promulgation; Ley 2080 de 2021: from publication).
- The source's earlier texts often leave out the article's epigraph (its title); where the latest earlier text differs from today's only by that or by a change no note names, today's text is used from the latest named act's day. - Constitutional Court rulings that struck text are laws of kind 'court', dated by the ruling's day as the source gives it; rulings that upheld text on a condition are court laws with a note and change no words.
- In-force days of amending acts: the act's own vigencia clause as its basedoc page gives it; otherwise the default rule (Ley 4 de 1913, art. 52: two months after promulgation). A day a provision's own note gives applies to that provision. The list below gives the day and the rule for each act.
- Dates come only from the act itself: the Diario Oficial day on the act's own page wins over a day the code's notes give; a note's Diario Oficial day is not given to an act named only inside another act's quoted title; and an act whose vigencia clause has a general rule and exceptions is dated by the rule that covers the changed provision (Ley 890 de 2004: arts. 7 to 13 immediately, the rest from 1 January 2005; Ley 2502 de 2025: art. 296 of the Código Penal one year after promulgation; Ley 2080 de 2021: from publication).

- Constitutional Court rulings that struck text are laws of kind 'court', dated by the ruling's day as the source gives it; rulings that upheld text on a condition are court laws with a note and change no words.
- In-force days of amending acts: the act's own vigencia clause as its basedoc page gives it; otherwise the default rule (Ley 4 de 1913, art. 52: two months after promulgation). A day a provision's own note gives applies to that provision. The list below gives the day and the rule for each act.
- Dates come only from the act itself: the Diario Oficial day on the act's own page wins over a day the code's notes give; a note's Diario Oficial day is not given to an act named only inside another act's quoted title; and an act whose vigencia clause has a general rule and exceptions is dated by the rule that covers the changed provision (Ley 890 de 2004: arts. 7 to 13 immediately, the rest from 1 January 2005; Ley 2502 de 2025: art. 296 of the Código Penal one year after promulgation; Ley 2080 de 2021: from publication).

- Constitutional Court rulings that struck text are laws of kind 'court', dated by the ruling's day as the source gives it; rulings that upheld text on a condition are court laws with a note and change no words.
- In-force days of amending acts: the act's own vigencia clause as its basedoc page gives it; otherwise the default rule (Ley 4 de 1913, art. 52: two months after promulgation). A day a provision's own note gives applies to that provision. The list below gives the day and the rule for each act.
- Dates come only from the act itself: the Diario Oficial day on the act's own page wins over a day the code's notes give; a note's Diario Oficial day is not given to an act named only inside another act's quoted title; and an act whose vigencia clause has a general rule and exceptions is dated by the rule that covers the changed provision (Ley 890 de 2004: arts. 7 to 13 immediately, the rest from 1 January 2005; Ley 2502 de 2025: art. 296 of the Código Penal one year after promulgation; Ley 2080 de 2021: from publication).

- Constitutional Court rulings that struck text are laws of kind 'court', dated by the ruling's day as the source gives it; rulings that upheld text on a condition are court laws with a note and change no words.
- In-force days of amending acts: the act's own vigencia clause as its basedoc page gives it; otherwise the default rule (Ley 4 de 1913, art. 52: two months after promulgation). A day a provision's own note gives applies to that provision. The list below gives the day and the rule for each act.
- Dates come only from the act itself: the Diario Oficial day on the act's own page wins over a day the code's notes give; a note's Diario Oficial day is not given to an act named only inside another act's quoted title; and an act whose vigencia clause has a general rule and exceptions is dated by the rule that covers the changed provision (Ley 890 de 2004: arts. 7 to 13 immediately, the rest from 1 January 2005; Ley 2502 de 2025: art. 296 of the Código Penal one year after promulgation; Ley 2080 de 2021: from publication).

- Deferral ends (2026-11-01): Código de Régimen Municipal (Decreto 1333 de 1986), art. 233 literal a) (the municipal tax on taking sand, gravel and stone from river beds): Sentencia C-221 de 1997 (29 April 1997; the page's box dates it 1999, a slip the ruling's own page corrects) held it EXEQUIBLE only for five (5) years from the ruling's notification, urged Congress to set within that term the royalties for the non-renewable resources not yet subject to one, and ordered that the literal becomes INEXEQUIBLE once such a law is issued within the term, or else when the term ends. The editor's notes point to Ley 685 de 2001 (Código de Minas, in force 8 September 2001, within the term), whose art. 11 makes river sand, gravel and stones 'materiales de construcción' and whose art. 227 makes every exploitation of State-owned non-renewable resources owe a royalty without setting its rate, and to art. 16 of Ley 756 de 2002 (25 July 2002), which first set a royalty for 'Materiales de construcción' (1%) but falls within the term only if the ruling was notified on or after 25 July 1997. Neither law certainly set those royalties within the term, so the literal leaves on 29 April 2002, the ruling's day plus five years, the earliest day the term can end (which has passed), credited to the ruling: the exact day depends on the notification day, which no source gives. Its letter stays, as for art. 252 c). The page still prints the literal with no marker; it had been kept to today.

Where the source names an act but gives no text after it, the article reads '[La fuente no da el texto vigente en esta fecha.]' for that period.
- Constitutional Court rulings that struck text are laws of kind 'court', dated by the ruling's day as the source gives it; rulings that upheld text on a condition are court laws with a note and change no words.
- In-force days of amending acts: the act's own vigencia clause as its basedoc page gives it; otherwise the default rule (Ley 4 de 1913, art. 52: two months after promulgation). A day a provision's own note gives applies to that provision. The list below gives the day and the rule for each act.
- Dates come only from the act itself: the Diario Oficial day on the act's own page wins over a day the code's notes give; a note's Diario Oficial day is not given to an act named only inside another act's quoted title; and an act whose vigencia clause has a general rule and exceptions is dated by the rule that covers the changed provision (Ley 890 de 2004: arts. 7 to 13 immediately, the rest from 1 January 2005; Ley 2502 de 2025: art. 296 of the Código Penal one year after promulgation; Ley 2080 de 2021: from publication).

- Sistema General de Regalías (Ley 2056 de 2020), Integración social de las personas con limitación (Ley 361 de 1997), Teletrabajo (Ley 1221 de 2008), Trabajo en casa (Ley 2088 de 2021), Trabajo remoto (Ley 2121 de 2021), Ley de Salud Mental (Ley 1616 de 2013), Transparencia, prevención y lucha contra la corrupción (Ley 2195 de 2022), Racionalización de trámites (Ley 2052 de 2020), Sanciones para condenados por corrupción (Ley 2014 de 2019), Sistema Nacional de Discapacidad (Ley 1145 de 2007): versions are rebuilt per article from the basedoc's earlier texts, inline amendment markers and Notas de Vigencia, as for the Constitution and the Código Civil. Where the source names an act but gives no text after it, the article reads '[La fuente no da el texto vigente en esta fecha.]' for that period.
- Constitutional Court rulings that struck text are laws of kind 'court', dated by the ruling's day as the source gives it; rulings that upheld text on a condition are court laws with a note and change no words.
- In-force days of amending acts: the act's own vigencia clause as its basedoc page gives it; otherwise the default rule (Ley 4 de 1913, art. 52: two months after promulgation). A day a provision's own note gives applies to that provision. The list below gives the day and the rule for each act.
- Dates come only from the act itself: the Diario Oficial day on the act's own page wins over a day the code's notes give; a note's Diario Oficial day is not given to an act named only inside another act's quoted title; and an act whose vigencia clause has a general rule and exceptions is dated by the rule that covers the changed provision (Ley 890 de 2004: arts. 7 to 13 immediately, the rest from 1 January 2005; Ley 2502 de 2025: art. 296 of the Código Penal one year after promulgation; Ley 2080 de 2021: from publication).
- The source's earlier texts often leave out the article's epigraph (its title); where the latest earlier text differs from today's only by that or by a change no note names, today's text is used from the latest named act's day. Articles where that happened: ley_1616_2013 art-0005, ley_2014_2019 art-0006, ley_2195_2022 art-0065.

- Conditional ruling notes (2026-11-01): Sentencia C-935 de 2013 upheld these provisions on a condition of interpretation (exequibilidad condicionada) and changed no words of them: SND Art. 16 on 2013-12-11. The same ruling also struck or replaced words in this record, so its law entry carries no note.
- Reforma financiera y régimen de protección al consumidor financiero (Ley 1328 de 2009), Ley del Mercado de Valores (Ley 964 de 2005), Reforma del sistema general de pensiones (Ley 797 de 2003), Factura como título valor (Ley 1231 de 2008), Servicios financieros transaccionales (Ley 1735 de 2014), Conglomerados financieros (Ley 1870 de 2017), Sistema financiero y asegurador (Ley 510 de 1999), Ley General de Desarrollo Agropecuario y Pesquero (Ley 101 de 1993), Zonas de Interés de Desarrollo Rural, Económico y Social (Ley 1776 de 2016): versions are rebuilt per article from the basedoc's earlier texts, inline amendment markers and Notas de Vigencia, as for the Constitution and the Código Civil. Where the source names an act but gives no text after it, the article reads '[La fuente no da el texto vigente en esta fecha.]' for that period.
- Constitutional Court rulings that struck text are laws of kind 'court', dated by the ruling's day as the source gives it; rulings that upheld text on a condition are court laws with a note and change no words.
- In-force days of amending acts: the act's own vigencia clause as its basedoc page gives it; otherwise the default rule (Ley 4 de 1913, art. 52: two months after promulgation). A day a provision's own note gives applies to that provision. The list below gives the day and the rule for each act.
- Dates come only from the act itself: the Diario Oficial day on the act's own page wins over a day the code's notes give; a note's Diario Oficial day is not given to an act named only inside another act's quoted title; and an act whose vigencia clause has a general rule and exceptions is dated by the rule that covers the changed provision (Ley 890 de 2004: arts. 7 to 13 immediately, the rest from 1 January 2005; Ley 2502 de 2025: art. 296 of the Código Penal one year after promulgation; Ley 2080 de 2021: from publication).
- The source's earlier texts often leave out the article's epigraph (its title); where the latest earlier text differs from today's only by that or by a change no note names, today's text is used from the latest named act's day. Articles where that happened: ley_0101_1993 art-0052, ley_0101_1993 art-0053, ley_0101_1993 art-0063, ley_0510_1999 art-0052, ley_0510_1999 art-0091.

- Constitutional Court rulings that struck text are laws of kind 'court', dated by the ruling's day as the source gives it; rulings that upheld text on a condition are court laws with a note and change no words.
- In-force days of amending acts: the act's own vigencia clause as its basedoc page gives it; otherwise the default rule (Ley 4 de 1913, art. 52: two months after promulgation). A day a provision's own note gives applies to that provision. The list below gives the day and the rule for each act.
- Dates come only from the act itself: the Diario Oficial day on the act's own page wins over a day the code's notes give; a note's Diario Oficial day is not given to an act named only inside another act's quoted title; and an act whose vigencia clause has a general rule and exceptions is dated by the rule that covers the changed provision (Ley 890 de 2004: arts. 7 to 13 immediately, the rest from 1 January 2005; Ley 2502 de 2025: art. 296 of the Código Penal one year after promulgation; Ley 2080 de 2021: from publication).

- Ley Sandra Ceballos, atención integral del cáncer (Ley 1384 de 2010), Ley Consuelo Devis Saavedra, cuidados paliativos (Ley 1733 de 2014), Prevención del consumo de tabaco (Ley 1335 de 2009), Atención integral a personas que consumen sustancias psicoactivas (Ley 1566 de 2012), Obesidad y enfermedades crónicas no transmisibles (Ley 1355 de 2009), Enfermedades huérfanas (Ley 1392 de 2010), Enfermedades ruinosas o catastróficas, VIH/Sida (Ley 972 de 2005), Donación de componentes anatómicos (Ley 1805 de 2016), Talento humano en salud (Ley 1164 de 2007), Protección de las personas que padecen epilepsia (Ley 1414 de 2010): versions are rebuilt per article from the basedoc's earlier texts, inline amendment markers and Notas de Vigencia, as for the Constitution and the Código Civil. - Constitutional Court rulings that struck text are laws of kind 'court', dated by the ruling's day as the source gives it; rulings that upheld text on a condition are court laws with a note and change no words.
- In-force days of amending acts: the act's own vigencia clause as its basedoc page gives it; otherwise the default rule (Ley 4 de 1913, art. 52: two months after promulgation). A day a provision's own note gives applies to that provision. The list below gives the day and the rule for each act.
- Dates come only from the act itself: the Diario Oficial day on the act's own page wins over a day the code's notes give; a note's Diario Oficial day is not given to an act named only inside another act's quoted title; and an act whose vigencia clause has a general rule and exceptions is dated by the rule that covers the changed provision (Ley 890 de 2004: arts. 7 to 13 immediately, the rest from 1 January 2005; Ley 2502 de 2025: art. 296 of the Código Penal one year after promulgation; Ley 2080 de 2021: from publication).

- Declared-INEXEQUIBLE articles (2026-11-01): the page marks the whole article '<Artículo declarado INEXEQUIBLE>', a whole-article strike that had been read only in the form '<Artículo INEXEQUIBLE>', so the article had stood in no version. Its text as enacted (the page's 'Texto original' box) now stands from the act's first day until the ruling, which takes it out and is credited: Código de Régimen Departamental (Decreto 1222 de 1986) art. 59 (Sentencia C-959 de 1999, 1999-12-01; the page's Jurisprudencia note reads 'declarado EXEQUIBLE', but the ruling's operative part reads 'Declarar INEXEQUIBLE el artículo 59 del Decreto 1222 de 1986', as the page's own marker says).
- Ejercicio de la psicología y Código Deontológico y Bioético (Ley 1090 de 2006), Empleo y emprendimiento juvenil (Ley 1780 de 2016), Fajas de retiro de las carreteras y Sistema Integral Nacional de Información de Carreteras (Ley 1228 de 2008), Protección del comprador de vivienda y seguridad de las edificaciones (Ley 1796 de 2016), Vivienda y hábitat (Ley 2079 de 2021), Voto programático (Ley 131 de 1994), Trata de personas (Ley 985 de 2005), Comisarías de Familia (Ley 2126 de 2021), Política de Estado para el Desarrollo Integral de la Primera Infancia de Cero a Siempre (Ley 1804 de 2016), Política pública social para habitantes de la calle (Ley 1641 de 2013): versions are rebuilt per article from the basedoc's earlier texts, inline amendment markers and Notas de Vigencia, as for the Constitution and the Código Civil. Where the source names an act but gives no text after it, the article reads '[La fuente no da el texto vigente en esta fecha.]' for that period.
- Constitutional Court rulings that struck text are laws of kind 'court', dated by the ruling's day as the source gives it; rulings that upheld text on a condition are court laws with a note and change no words.
- In-force days of amending acts: the act's own vigencia clause as its basedoc page gives it; otherwise the default rule (Ley 4 de 1913, art. 52: two months after promulgation). A day a provision's own note gives applies to that provision. The list below gives the day and the rule for each act.
- Dates come only from the act itself: the Diario Oficial day on the act's own page wins over a day the code's notes give; a note's Diario Oficial day is not given to an act named only inside another act's quoted title; and an act whose vigencia clause has a general rule and exceptions is dated by the rule that covers the changed provision (Ley 890 de 2004: arts. 7 to 13 immediately, the rest from 1 January 2005; Ley 2502 de 2025: art. 296 of the Código Penal one year after promulgation; Ley 2080 de 2021: from publication).
- The source's earlier texts often leave out the article's epigraph (its title); where the latest earlier text differs from today's only by that or by a change no note names, today's text is used from the latest named act's day. Articles where that happened: none.

(...)', the editor's abbreviation in the original-text box.
- Dated-struck audit, hand entries (2026-10-31): words the page shows struck or replaced, which the engine had left out of the versions they belong to (the text before the change differs from today's, the source's earlier text was not known, or the page marks a substitution), were put back by hand from the page's own struck words, notes and rulings box, each in the versions its entry names; on the day the page gives they go or change, credited to the ruling or act that made the change: Plan Nacional de Desarrollo 2022-2026 (Ley 2294 de 2023) art. 210: 'no sociales' and 'o por la Agencia Nacional para la Reincorporación y la Normalización', which Sentencia C-037-23 (2023-02-23) had struck from the text of Ley 2197 de 2022, were enacted again by Ley 2294 de 2023 (this article, amending art. 91 of Ley 1708 de 2014) and stand from 2023-05-19: words Congress re-enacts are in force from the re-enactment until a ruling strikes them again, and the page names no ruling on Ley 2294's words (C-448-24 and C-143-25 upheld the article); the page prints them struck under C-037-23's marker.
- Re-enacted words (coordinator decision, 2026-10-31): words a ruling had struck from an earlier text and that Congress enacts again are in force from the re-enactment's day until a ruling strikes them again; the page prints them struck under the earlier ruling's marker. Applied to 'no sociales' and 'o por la Agencia Nacional para la Reincorporación y la Normalización' (Sentencia C-037-23 on Ley 2197 de 2022's text of art. 91 of Ley 1708 de 2014), enacted again by Ley 2294 de 2023 art. 210 and in force from 2023-05-19 to today: the page names no ruling on Ley 2294's words.
- Strikes on their own rulings' days (2026-11-01): where several Constitutional Court rulings struck different words of one provision, each ruling's words now go on that ruling's day, as the page's Jurisprudencia Vigencia box ties them (the line quoting the words, or the box printed right after their paragraph); the engine had put all of them on the latest ruling's day: Plan Nacional de Desarrollo 2022-2026 (Ley 2294 de 2023) art. 372: 'el artículo 52 de la Ley 2136 de 2021' out on 2 April 2025, credited to Sentencia C-119 de 2025 (the rulings box quotes the words under that ruling).
- Derecho fundamental de petición (Ley 1755 de 2015), Reforma laboral (Ley 2466 de 2025), Plan Nacional de Desarrollo 2018-2022 (Ley 1955 de 2019): versions are rebuilt per article from the basedoc's earlier texts, inline amendment markers and Notas de Vigencia, as for the Constitution and the Código Civil. Where the source names an act but gives no text after it, the article reads '[La fuente no da el texto vigente en esta fecha.]' for that period.
- Constitutional Court rulings that struck text are laws of kind 'court', dated by the ruling's day as the source gives it; rulings that upheld text on a condition are court laws with a note and change no words.
- In-force days of amending acts: the act's own vigencia clause as its basedoc page gives it; otherwise the default rule (Ley 4 de 1913, art. 52: two months after promulgation). A day a provision's own note gives applies to that provision. The list below gives the day and the rule for each act.
- Dates come only from the act itself: the Diario Oficial day on the act's own page wins over a day the code's notes give; a note's Diario Oficial day is not given to an act named only inside another act's quoted title; and an act whose vigencia clause has a general rule and exceptions is dated by the rule that covers the changed provision (Ley 890 de 2004: arts. 7 to 13 immediately, the rest from 1 January 2005; Ley 2502 de 2025: art. 296 of the Código Penal one year after promulgation; Ley 2080 de 2021: from publication).
- The source's earlier texts often leave out the article's epigraph (its title); where the latest earlier text differs from today's only by that or by a change no note names, today's text is used from the latest named act's day. Articles where that happened: none.
- Derecho fundamental de petición (Ley 1755 de 2015): first version from 2015-06-30: Ley 1755 de 2015, art. 2: 'La presente ley rige a partir de la fecha de su promulgación y deroga las disposiciones que le sean contrarias.' (sanctioned 2015-06-30, Diario Oficial of 2015-06-30)
- Reforma laboral (Ley 2466 de 2025): first version from 2025-06-25: Ley 2466 de 2025, art. 70: 'La presente ley rige a partir de su promulgación y deroga o modifica todas las que le sean contrarias o incompatibles. - Plan Nacional de Desarrollo 2018-2022 (Ley 1955 de 2019): first version from 2019-05-25: Ley 1955 de 2019, art. 336: 'La presente ley rige a partir de su publicación y deroga todas las disposiciones que le sean contrarias. Los artículos de las Leyes 812 de 2003, 1151 de 2007, 1450 de 2011, y 1753 de 2015 no derogados expresamente en el siguiente Inciso o por otras leyes continuarán vigentes hasta que sean derogados o modificados por norma posterior. [...]' (sanctioned 2019-05-25, Diario Oficial of 2019-05-25)
- Plan Nacional de Desarrollo 2018-2022 (Ley 1955 de 2019): Ley 1955 de 2019: art. 130's earlier text is headed 'Texto original de la Ley 1955 de 2022'; it is the act's own original article (of 2019).
- Plan Nacional de Desarrollo 2018-2022 (Ley 1955 de 2019): Ley 1955 de 2019: art. 313's earlier text is headed 'Texto original de la Ley 1955 de 2020'; it is the act's own original article (of 2019).
- Derecho fundamental de petición (Ley 1755 de 2015) and the other acts of batch 38: an article an act repealed as a whole, whose last words the page still prints after the marker '<Artículo derogado por el artículo N de la Ley X>' and which has no earlier-text box, reads those words from the act's first day until the repeal, and is gone from it: ley_1955_2019 art-0163 (Ley 2294 de 2023).
- Reforma laboral (Ley 2466 de 2025): Ley 2466 de 2025, arts. 24 to 30 (trabajo en plataformas digitales de reparto): art. 67 says they 'comenzarán a regir doce (12) meses después de que el Gobierno nacional cumpla con las obligaciones de reglamentación e implementación allí señaladas', and each is printed under that marker. The source dates no such regulation, so their start day is unknown: they are in no version (open item: add them from their start day once a dated regulation fixes it).
- Plan Nacional de Desarrollo 2018-2022 (Ley 1955 de 2019): Ley 1955 de 2019: articles the page prints under '<Artículo INEXEQUIBLE ...>' markers, which the engine left out of every version. Their printed words are the text from the act's first day until the ruling takes effect: art. 18 until Sentencia C-484-20 (19 November 2020; the words of numeral 4 the page shows struck, 'y todos aquellos que inciden directa o indirectamente en la prestación de los servicios públicos domiciliarios', out from Sentencia C-464-20 of 28 October 2020, the ruling's day, although the marker says 'desde el 20 de octubre de 2020'); art. 314 until Sentencia C-147-21 (20 May 2021, immediate effect; C-464-20 had struck it from 1 January 2023); art. 193 until 20 June 2023 (Sentencia C-276-21 of 19 August 2021, effect deferred to that day).
- Plan Nacional de Desarrollo 2018-2022 (Ley 1955 de 2019): Ley 1955 de 2019, art. 244 (ingreso base de cotización de los independientes), struck by Sentencia C-068-20 (19 February 2020) with effect deferred to 21 July 2022: the incisos and the parágrafo the page prints from the act's first day; parágrafo 2 as Ley 2010 de 2019 (art. 139) added it (the earlier-text box) from 27 December 2019; its wording as Decreto 690 de 2020 corrected it (today's printed words) from that decree's day; the article out from 21 July 2022. The engine had only parágrafo 2, from 2019.
- Plan Nacional de Desarrollo 2018-2022 (Ley 1955 de 2019): Ley 1955 de 2019, art. 49 (cálculo de valores en UVT): the page marks it '<Artículo derogado a partir del 1 de enero de 2024 por el artículo 372 de la Ley 2294 de 2023>' and prints its words, with no earlier text: those words from the act's first day, the article out from 1 January 2024, credited to Ley 2294 de 2023 (the engine had a placeholder until 2023 and the words to today).

- Sistema de Protección Social Integral para la Vejez, Invalidez y Muerte (Ley 2381 de 2024): Ley 2381 de 2024 (pension reform). Art. 95: 'la presente ley rige a partir de su sanción' (16 July 2024); art. 94 put the Sistema de Protección Social Integral para la Vejez in force on 1 July 2025; Auto A-841-25 of 27 June 2025 suspended that, except art. 12's parágrafo transitorio and art. 76 (both run from the law's issue: six months to choose an administrator, two years to change regime); Sentencia C-264-26 (25 August 2026) upheld the articles it reviewed, 'Entra en vigencia a partir del 1 de abril de 2027'. History: from 16 July 2024 the act holds art. 12's parágrafo transitorio (under the article's epigraph), art. 76 and arts. 94 and 95; on 1 April 2027 (the future branch) the rest of the text the page prints, except the provisions C-264-26 returned to the Cámara de Representantes, whose entry into force depends on a procedure not yet done: art. 63 inciso 2, art. 84 numeral 5, art. 92 inciso 1 and art. 93.

- Dates come only from the act itself: the Diario Oficial day on the act's own page wins over a day the code's notes give; a note's Diario Oficial day is not given to an act named only inside another act's quoted title; and an act whose vigencia clause has a general rule and exceptions is dated by the rule that covers the changed provision (Ley 890 de 2004: arts. 7 to 13 immediately, the rest from 1 January 2005; Ley 2502 de 2025: art. 296 of the Código Penal one year after promulgation; Ley 2080 de 2021: from publication).

- In-force days of amending acts: the act's own vigencia clause as its basedoc page gives it; otherwise the default rule (Ley 4 de 1913, art. 52: two months after promulgation). A day a provision's own note gives applies to that provision. The list below gives the day and the rule for each act.
- Dates come only from the act itself: the Diario Oficial day on the act's own page wins over a day the code's notes give; a note's Diario Oficial day is not given to an act named only inside another act's quoted title; and an act whose vigencia clause has a general rule and exceptions is dated by the rule that covers the changed provision (Ley 890 de 2004: arts. 7 to 13 immediately, the rest from 1 January 2005; Ley 2502 de 2025: art. 296 of the Código Penal one year after promulgation; Ley 2080 de 2021: from publication).
- The source's earlier texts often leave out the article's epigraph (its title); where the latest earlier text differs from today's only by that or by a change no note names, today's text is used from the latest named act's day. Articles where that happened: none.

- Reestructuración empresarial (Ley 550 de 1999): first version from 1999-12-30: Ley 550 de 1999, art. 79: 'Esta ley regirá durante cinco (5) años, contados a partir la fecha de su publicación en el Diario Oficial, y durante el mismo plazo se aplicará de preferencia sobre cualquier norma legal, incluidas las tributarias, que le sean contrarias. De conformidad con el artículo 38 de la Ley 153 de 1887, las disposiciones de esta ley se entienden incorporadas en los acuerdos de reestructuración que lleven a celebrarse legalmente durante su vigencia, por lo cual se ejecutarán con sujeción a lo dispuesto en ella, al igual que los demás actos y contratos que se celebren en desarrollo de los mismos. El parágrafo primero del artículo 14 de esta ley sólo se aplica a las garantías de terceros otorgadas con posterioridad a su entrada en vigencia. Las garantías preexistentes sólo podrán hacerse efectivas si transcurrido el plazo previsto en el artículo 27 de esta ley no se celebra un acuerdo; mientras tanto, podrán practicarse medidas cautelares; y la iniciación y la continuación de procesos judiciales contra el garante, al igual que la ejecución de las garantías reales o fiduciarias, se sujetarán a lo dispuesto en el literal b) del parágrafo segundo del artículo 14 de esta ley. El parágrafo segundo del artículo 14 de esta ley se aplica respecto de garantes personas naturales que hayan otorgado la garantía antes o después de la vigencia de esta ley.' First published in Diario Oficial No. 43.836 of 1999-12-30; republished to correct transcription errors in Diario Oficial No. 43.940 of 2000-03-19, whose text is the one given here.
- Régimen de sociedades (Ley 222 de 1995): first version from 1996-06-20: Ley 222 de 1995, art. 237: 'Esta ley empezará a regir al vencimiento de los seis meses contados a partir de su promulgación. Los concordatos y las quiebras iniciadas antes de la entrada en vigencia de esta ley, seguirán rigiéndose por las normas aplicables al momento de entrar a regir esta Ley. No obstante, esta Ley se aplicará inmediatamente entre en vigencia, en los siguientes casos: 1. Cuando fracase o se incumpla el concordato, en cuyo evento, en vez de la quiebra se adelantará la liquidación obligatoria. 2. En lo relacionado con el decreto, práctica y levantamiento de las medidas cautelares consagrados en esta Ley.' (six months after promulgation in the Diario Oficial of 1995-12-20)

- Dates come only from the act itself: the Diario Oficial day on the act's own page wins over a day the code's notes give; a note's Diario Oficial day is not given to an act named only inside another act's quoted title; and an act whose vigencia clause has a general rule and exceptions is dated by the rule that covers the changed provision (Ley 890 de 2004: arts. 7 to 13 immediately, the rest from 1 January 2005; Ley 2502 de 2025: art. 296 of the Código Penal one year after promulgation; Ley 2080 de 2021: from publication).
- The source's earlier texts often leave out the article's epigraph (its title); where the latest earlier text differs from today's only by that or by a change no note names, today's text is used from the latest named act's day. Articles where that happened: none.

- Zonas de frontera (Ley 191 de 1995): the Jurisprudencia Vigencia boxes date Sentencia C-615 de 1996 '13 de noviembre de 1995'; the ruling's number (C-615-96) and the page's own link to it (c-615_1996.html) give 1996: read as 13 November 1996.
- Zonas de frontera (Ley 191 de 1995): art. 40: the page heads it '<Artículo modificado por el Artículo 1o. del Decreto 1182 de 1999 ... El texto original es el siguiente:>' and prints the words as enacted. That decree (Diario Oficial No. 43.626 of 29 June 1999), as its Notas de Vigencia quote it, abolished the Consejería Presidencial de Fronteras the article created and gave its functions to the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores; it changed no words of the article. The article reads as enacted from the act's first day to today, and the decree is no version (the engine had put the placeholder before it).
- Zonas de frontera (Ley 191 de 1995): art. 27 (IVA exemptions for goods from neighbouring countries, Amazonas): repealed by Ley 633 de 2000 art. 134 (29 December 2000). Ley 677 de 2001 art. 29 (4 August 2001) took out the words of art. 134 that repealed it, but did not re-enact the article: a repealed provision does not revive because the law that repealed it is abolished, only by being reproduced in a new law (Ley 153 de 1887, art. 14). The article is out from 29 December 2000; the page still prints its words under its repeal marker; they are the words as enacted (the engine had put the placeholder before the repeal and brought the words back on 4 August 2001).

Changes made inside the deferral stay where they touched words Ley 619 had not written: on art. 10, Sentencia C-427 de 2002 (29 May 2002) struck 'irresponsable o' in numeral 4, which Ley 619 had not touched (the ruling's box stands under numeral 4): that strike stays, while numeral 1, which Ley 619 had rewritten, takes its earlier words back. Art. 13, which Ley 619 repealed (tacitly, Sentencia C-672 de 2002), is back from 20 June 2002 and out again from 25 July 2002: the Court held it 'hubiera recobrado vigencia si no hubiera sido expedida la Ley 756 de 2002'. Art. 62's text before Ley 619, which only added its parágrafo, is the article without that parágrafo (from the act's first day as well). The engine had brought the earlier words back on the ruling's day for nine articles and never for the other seven. (Arts. 1, 5, 9, 16 and 29 follow the same rule within the full histories set for them below.)

- Reforma tributaria (Ley 633 de 2000): art. 1 adds Libro Sexto (Gravamen a los Movimientos Financieros, ET arts. 870 to 881) to the Estatuto Tributario. The page gives each quoted ET article its own anchor with the ET's later notes. As for Ley 1607 de 2012 (coordinator decision): the quoted articles are the text of art. 1 as enacted, read inside it as quoted text with no separate units and none of the ET's later notes or rulings on them; ET art. 879 reads the page's copy of the article as enacted (the page first prints Ley 1739 de 2014's numeral 1). Their later fate is the Estatuto Tributario's history.
- Reforma tributaria (Ley 488 de 1998): arts. 30 and 84 rewrite ET arts. 249 and 362, which the page gives their own anchors; read the same way, as quoted text inside arts. 30 and 84.
- Reforma tributaria (Ley 488 de 1998): art. 145 (impuesto sobre vehículos automotores, tarifas): the page prints today's brackets, the values Decreto 1457 de 2025 set for 2026, as a table; they are read as the lines the page's earlier-text boxes print ('a) Hasta $... 1,5%'), under '1. Vehículos particulares:' (the page's repeated 'Vehículos particulares:' line before the table is left out).
- Reforma tributaria (Ley 633 de 2000): art. 4: the page marks the whole article '<Artículo declarado INEXEQUIBLE>' (struck by Sentencia C-992-01). Its text as enacted (the page's 'Texto original' box, with the epigraph the page prints in the article's heading) stands from the act's first day until the ruling (2001-09-19).
- Reforma tributaria (Ley 633 de 2000): Ley 633 de 2000, art. 80 (subsidio de energía para distritos de riego): each year's budget law rewrote it tacitly ('Para el año 2022 debe entenderse modificado tácitamente por el artículo 100 de la Ley 2159 de 2021 ...'). The page's last boxes head two texts 'Texto modificado tácitamente por la Ley 2063 de 2020': the one whose parágrafo 3o. says the subsidy runs from 1 January 2021 is Ley 2063 de 2020's; the other (parágrafo 3o. 'El Gobierno nacional deberá reglamentar ...') is the 2022 text, which the page's notes give to Ley 2159 de 2021. The engine read both as one and gave today's text (Ley 2276 de 2022, for 2023) from Ley 2063's day. Now: Ley 2063's text from its day, Ley 2159's from its day, today's from Ley 2276's. The Ley 2008 de 2019 box prints the page's marker inside the text ('Para el año 2020 modificado tácitamente por el artículo 125 de la Ley 2008 de 2019. El nuevo texto es el siguiente:>'); those words are left out.
- Reforma tributaria (Ley 633 de 2000): Ley 633 de 2000, art. 80, 2009 (coordinator decision): Ley 1152 de 2007 (Estatuto de Desarrollo Rural, art. 112) tacitly rewrote the article from 25 July 2007, and Sentencia C-175-09 (18 March 2009) struck Ley 1152 as a whole. Under the corpus's rule that a struck law's predecessor text does not revive by itself, from the ruling's day the article reads the placeholder '[La fuente no da el texto vigente en esta fecha.]', credited to the ruling, until Ley 1365 de 2009 (art. 89) rewrote it again (21 December 2009); the page gives no text for those months (Ley 1260 de 2008, the 2009 budget, did not include it).
- Reforma tributaria (Ley 633 de 2000): Ley 633 de 2000, art. 58 (empresas asociativas de trabajo, Ley 10 de 1991 art. 16 as rewritten): the page's boxes give the amounts as enacted ($400.000.000 / $200.000.000), for 2002 (Decreto 2794 de 2001: $432.300.000 / $216.200.000) and for 2003 (Decreto 3257 de 2002: $458.300.000 / $229.100.000; a second box headed only 'Texto original de la Ley 633 de 2000' repeats them); today's text gives those for 2004 (Decreto 3804 de 2003). The engine gave each box's amounts to the decree before it (the 2003 amounts as enacted). Now each set stands from 1 January of its year, credited to its decree, in today's words (the boxes quote the rewritten article with single quotes and leave out its opening 'Modifícase el artículo 16 de la Ley 10 de 1991, el cual quedará así:').
- Reforma tributaria (Ley 633 de 2000): Ley 633 de 2000, art. 134 (vigencia y derogatorias): the page strikes 'el artículo 27 de la Ley 191 de 1995' in the list of repealed provisions, with the marker '<Aparte tachado suprimido por el artículo 29 de la Ley 677 de 2001>' (Diario Oficial No. 44.509 of 4 August 2001); the engine left the struck words out of every version. They stand from the act's first day until Ley 677 de 2001 takes them out, credited to it.
- Reforma tributaria (Ley 633 de 2000): Ley 633 de 2000, art. 91 (páginas web): Sentencia C-1147-01 ('de octubre 31 de 2001', the month written first) upheld the article on a condition and struck the words the page shows struck; the engine left those words out of the 2000 version too (the ruling's day changed no words). They stand from the act's first day until the ruling.
- Reforma tributaria (Ley 488 de 1998): Ley 488 de 1998, art. 48 (Estatuto Tributario art. 476 as rewritten), numeral 21: the page writes 'a 31 de diciembre {del año inmediatamente anterior}', braces its 'Legislación Anterior' boxes explain as words the decrees that updated the absolute values for 2003-2006 left out of their tables ('textos entre corchetes {...} omitidos por el Decreto ...'). A decree that updates values does not change a law's words: the words stand in every version, without the braces (as in the Estatuto Tributario's own history).

- Reforma tributaria (Ley 488 de 1998): Ley 488 de 1998, art. 48 (Estatuto Tributario art. 476), numeral 21 (added by Ley 788 de 2002): the page's boxes give its values for each year from 2003 to 2006; the engine left out the last box (the values Decreto 4715 de 2005 set for 2006, '$3.576.812.000' and '$596.135.000') and gave the numeral's UVT wording from 1 January 2006, though Ley 1111 de 2006 (27 December 2006) put the values in UVT ('ajusta los valores absolutos en términos de UVT', the page's note). - Reforma tributaria (Ley 488 de 1998): Ley 488 de 1998, art. 80 (creación de la policía fiscal y aduanera): the page's marker '<Artículo derogado por el artículo 53 la Ley 633 de 2001<sic, 2000>, según establece la Corte Constitucional en Sentencias C-1066-01>' holds a marker inside a marker, so its tail stood as the article's text in every version. The text as enacted (the page's 'Texto original' box, whose heading misprints 'ARTÍCULO 81.' and whose last line ends in a stray quote) stands from the act's first day; Ley 633 de 2000 (art. 53, which the Court read as repealing it: C-1066-01) takes it out on its day, 29 December 2000.
- Reforma tributaria (Ley 488 de 1998): Ley 488 de 1998, art. 100 (gasolina en zonas fronterizas): repealed by Ley 681 de 2001 (10 August 2001), so the page prints no current text and the act's first version had held a placeholder. - Reforma tributaria (Ley 488 de 1998): Ley 488 de 1998, art. 91: Ley 633 de 2000 art. 99 rewrote it (29 December 2000) and Sentencia C-992-01 (19 September 2001) struck parts of that wording; the 2000 version held a placeholder. - Reforma tributaria (Ley 488 de 1998): Ley 488 de 1998, art. 121 (base gravable de la sobretasa): Sentencia C-030-19 (30 January 2019) struck the inciso with its effects 'diferidos por el término de dos legislaturas a partir de la fecha de notificación' (notified by edicto on 13 March 2019). The two legislatures after that day are 2019-2020 and 2020-2021; the second ends on 20 June 2021 (Constitución art. 138), so the inciso goes on that day, credited to the ruling (as Sentencia C-161-24's deferral by two legislatures, batch 91). The page still prints it under its marker '<Inciso INEXEQUIBLE, efectos diferidos por dos legislaturas>'; Ley 2093 de 2021 (29 June 2021) then added art. 121A, a new base gravable.

Where the source names an act but gives no text after it, the article reads '[La fuente no da el texto vigente en esta fecha.]' for that period.
- Constitutional Court rulings that struck text are laws of kind 'court', dated by the ruling's day as the source gives it; rulings that upheld text on a condition are court laws with a note and change no words.
- In-force days of amending acts: the act's own vigencia clause as its basedoc page gives it; otherwise the default rule (Ley 4 de 1913, art. 52: two months after promulgation). A day a provision's own note gives applies to that provision. The list below gives the day and the rule for each act.
- Dates come only from the act itself: the Diario Oficial day on the act's own page wins over a day the code's notes give; a note's Diario Oficial day is not given to an act named only inside another act's quoted title; and an act whose vigencia clause has a general rule and exceptions is dated by the rule that covers the changed provision (Ley 890 de 2004: arts. 7 to 13 immediately, the rest from 1 January 2005; Ley 2502 de 2025: art. 296 of the Código Penal one year after promulgation; Ley 2080 de 2021: from publication).
- The source's earlier texts often leave out the article's epigraph (its title); where the latest earlier text differs from today's only by that or by a change no note names, today's text is used from the latest named act's day. Articles where that happened: none.

- Prórroga y reforma de la Ley 418 de 1997 (Ley 1421 de 2010): Ley 1421 de 2010, art. 8 (aportes voluntarios a los fondos-cuenta territoriales). (a) Sentencia C-891-12 (31 October 2012) struck the last inciso ('El carácter de los sujetos pasivos y la base impositiva del tributo serán reglamentados por el Ministerio del Interior y de Justicia.'), which the page gives only in its Legislación Anterior box under an empty '<Inciso INEXEQUIBLE>' marker: out from that day, credited to C-891-12 (the engine had taken it out on the day of Sentencia C-101-22, whose version is gone). (b) Sentencia C-101-22 (17 March 2022) struck the second inciso ('Los departamentos y municipios podrán imponer tasas o sobretasas especiales ...') and the third inciso of the parágrafo ('El inciso segundo del presente artículo no estará sometido a la vigencia de la prórroga ...') with its effects deferred by two legislatures from its notification (Edicto No. 48 of 1 June 2022); the second of those legislatures ends on 20 June 2024 (Constitución art. 138; the page's own note '<hasta 20 de junio de 2024>'), so both go on that day, credited to the ruling (as Sentencia C-030-19's deferral, batch 98). The page still prints both under the marker '<Inciso INEXEQUIBLE. Fallo diferido ...>'. Ley 2272 de 2022 art. 12 (Diario Oficial No. 52.208 of 4 November 2022), 'in compliance with' C-101-22, lets territories already collecting the tax go on doing so: a rule of its own that changes none of Ley 1421's words. No version. Sentencia C-045-18 (inhibited) changes nothing.

The engine had the placeholder from 2013 and the article out from the ruling's day. - Constitutional Court rulings that struck text are laws of kind 'court', dated by the ruling's day as the source gives it; rulings that upheld text on a condition are court laws with a note and change no words.

- Dates come only from the act itself: the Diario Oficial day on the act's own page wins over a day the code's notes give; a note's Diario Oficial day is not given to an act named only inside another act's quoted title; and an act whose vigencia clause has a general rule and exceptions is dated by the rule that covers the changed provision (Ley 890 de 2004: arts. 7 to 13 immediately, the rest from 1 January 2005; Ley 2502 de 2025: art. 296 of the Código Penal one year after promulgation; Ley 2080 de 2021: from publication).

- Constitutional Court rulings that struck text are laws of kind 'court', dated by the ruling's day as the source gives it; rulings that upheld text on a condition are court laws with a note and change no words.
- In-force days of amending acts: the act's own vigencia clause as its basedoc page gives it; otherwise the default rule (Ley 4 de 1913, art. 52: two months after promulgation). A day a provision's own note gives applies to that provision. The list below gives the day and the rule for each act.
- Dates come only from the act itself: the Diario Oficial day on the act's own page wins over a day the code's notes give; a note's Diario Oficial day is not given to an act named only inside another act's quoted title; and an act whose vigencia clause has a general rule and exceptions is dated by the rule that covers the changed provision (Ley 890 de 2004: arts. 7 to 13 immediately, the rest from 1 January 2005; Ley 2502 de 2025: art. 296 of the Código Penal one year after promulgation; Ley 2080 de 2021: from publication).
- The source's earlier texts often leave out the article's epigraph (its title); where the latest earlier text differs from today's only by that or by a change no note names, today's text is used from the latest named act's day. Articles where that happened: none.

## What AI did and did not do

The scripts that read the sources and build this repository were written by Claude Code running Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`) under Lexifina's direction.

No model wrote, translated or corrected legal text. No model runs at build time. Every word of law in this repository comes from the official sources above.

The commit messages are written by `build.py` from the source data.

Model use at data-build time:
- None at data-build time: Lexifina's code is deterministic code, written with Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5); no model reads, writes or summarises legal text. The README was drafted with the same tool.
